thread.old_title: The individual-mercy contrast cases — Elias, Eliseus, and the famine in Sirach 48
thread.title: Elijah's famine and Elisha's spirit — Sirach 48 behind the widow of Sidon and Naaman
thread.old_summary: At Natsareth (Nazareth) the King names the two contrast cases that turn the synagogue to murder-rage: *many widows were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the days of Elijah... but unto none of them was Elijah sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow. And many lepers were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the time of Elisha the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian* (Luke 4:25-27). These are the INDIVIDUAL-MERCY-WITHOUT-ABSORPTION cases the framework holds against the false-inclusion gospel: foreign-origin individuals — the Tsidonian (Sidonian) widow, the Syrian commander — receive mercy without being thereby made covenant-seed. Absorption into the seed-of-promise runs through the marriage-covenant alone (Rachav/Rahab, Ruth); the contrast cases prove the directional non-symmetry. The Hebrew library carries the prophets behind both cases. Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:1-3 names Eliyahu (Elijah) the fire-prophet who *by the word of Yahuah (God)... shut up the heaven* — the very famine the King names. Sirach 48:12 names *Elisha* (Elisha) *filled with his spirit* — the prophet who cleansed the Syrian. The crowd hears the contrast cases as a threat to the flesh-credential gospel of *we have Avraham (Abraham) to our father* and wants the King dead for it. The Hebrew library names the prophets; the King reads their individual-mercy cases as the tell that exposes the flesh-credential lie.
thread.summary:
It ain't new. The two names he sets before Nazareth are the two prophets Sirach praises back to back. Elijah first:

*Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* (Sirach 48:1)

*By the word of Yahuah (God) he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire.* (Sirach 48:3)

That shut heaven is the famine he names in the synagogue: *many widows were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months* (Luke 4:25). Then Elisha:

*Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: while he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.* (Sirach 48:12)

Filled with Elijah's spirit, and the one leper he cleansed was *Naaman the Syrian* (Luke 4:27). Sirach knows both prophets as Yashar'el (Israel)'s own and does nothing to soften where their work landed. In the famine the word went to a widow in Sidon, and the leper made clean was a Syrian, while many in the land went without. They were not strangers shown a favour; they were the ones who heard. *Now by this I know that thou art a man of Elohim (God), and that the word of Yahuah (LORD) in thy mouth is truth.* (1 Kings 17:24). *Behold, now I know that there is no Elohim (God) in all the earth, but in Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Kings 5:15). Seed of the house revealed outside its borders by its hearing, which is how his sheep are always known: *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:* (John 10:27). Nazareth heard the same two stories told back to them and *were filled with wrath* (Luke 4:28).
